note: Every published page, the area it sits in and its place in reading order (spec: kb.data.structure). An area is one hub: `nestUnder` names its parent, `hub` holds what the hub page says about itself, and `pages` lists its rows in reading order. A row's `slug` is the page's file name, `source` its markdown under docs/, and `route` its HTML path on the site, kept so every inbound URL survives (dialect D-02). A page's `area` frontmatter key is the id of the area that lists it. The `map` area is the one exception: its `generated` key names the program that writes its page at build time, and its row's `source` is `generated`, since no page under docs/ holds it. An area's optional `nav` key is closed: `link` makes a single-page area with no hub, shown as one top-level sidebar link to its only row, and `none` leaves the area unpublished (its rows, its hub and its sidebar group stay off the site, while the pages keep their `area` and their place in the docs map). The `map` area is `link`; its last area, reference, lists the hand-written pages under docs/reference/ and docs/concepts/ and is `none`. The single source, edited by hand (kb.mjs new adds a new page's row): the hub generator, gen-map (make map, or make gen) and the structure gate read it, the AREAS tuple in site/src/lib/types.ts lists its area ids in order, and moving a page means changing it and learning-paths.json together.
